$comment: Every Flexarr app and platform, shown at flexarr.io/apps and served as flexarr.io/apps.json. Edit this file, then run `make apps`. status: available | beta | coming | development | planned. Entries with "release": "server" get the server's version from scripts/release.sh; set the others by hand when a store build goes live.

groups.title: Watch and listen
groups.intro: Connect each app to your server once with a short code.

groups.title: Run it at home
groups.intro: One server holds your libraries and serves every app.

groups.title: Works with
groups.intro: Flexarr in the other things you use at home.

platforms.name: iPhone and iPad
platforms.summary: Downloads for offline, podcasts with widgets and alerts, Siri, Picture in Picture and AirPlay.

platforms.name: Apple TV
platforms.summary: Your libraries, music and live TV from the sofa, with Continue Watching in the Top Shelf and a player built for HDR and Atmos.
platforms.note: With Apple for review. Until it's on the App Store you can install it from a Mac.

platforms.name: Web
platforms.summary: Built into the server, nothing to install. Open your server's address on a computer, tablet or phone.

platforms.name: Android phone and tablet
platforms.summary: A native Android app for phones and tablets. Until it's ready, the web app works in your phone's browser.

platforms.name: Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV
platforms.summary: Flexarr on the big screen for TVs and streaming sticks that run Android.

platforms.name: Flexarr server
platforms.requires: Docker on Linux, Windows, Synology or Unraid (64-bit Intel, AMD or ARM), or a Mac
platforms.summary: Reads your films, TV, music and podcasts, works with Sonarr, Radarr and Lidarr, and streams to every app. Free for personal use.

platforms.name: Home Assistant
platforms.requires: Home Assistant with HACS, and Flexarr 0.45.0 or later
platforms.summary: Every Apple TV, iPhone and iPad becomes a media player, so your home can react to what you're watching: lights down when a film starts.
